ZWE.note: Satellite use in Zimbabwe is described only as FAO-supported precision agriculture; no government, agency or research service using satellite data is stated.
Nothing on rules or an authority for AI harms in Zimbabwe.
Chatbots with ministries of agriculture are described for Africa in general, not for Zimbabwe by name.

facts.fact: FAO says AI-enabled crop monitoring tools such as EOSTAT are improving the accuracy of crop statistics and yield predictions in Zimbabwe; the operating body is not named.

FAO says CROPFIX, an AI pest and disease diagnostic tool created by a Zimbabwean youth-led startup and trained on more than 25,000 local field images, is in use among thousands of smallholder farmers.

ZWE.note: No government technical staff or technology body is described.
The startup behind CROPFIX is named, but no startup law, labelling or public fund is stated.
No hub, incubator or park is described.
